failure_story: We treated AMD as a Data Center compounder on FY2025 owner cash of $3.37 per share while paying about $550, with proof-backed component value near $96 per share and Lawrence synthesis already negative at about -14.6% per year. The failure path was competitive and multiple-driven, not solvency: NVIDIA CUDA and custom ASIC programs capped Instinct share and pricing, Data Center growth decelerated from the +32% FY2025 pace, and Client/Gaming cyclicality returned. Trailing free cash flow per share failed to expand toward the AI-inflection sensitivity ($4.8/sh), foundry prepayments stayed elevated, and the market re-rated AMD from AI challenger to cyclical semiconductor. Selling multiples compressed; hold-period return landed near the contract bear envelope (about -25% annualized) as the gap between $550 and ~$96 component value closed. Equity de-rating on a partial-dhando name was the primary capital-loss path.
